correctness.rationale: The exact horocycle criterion follows from monotonicity of a Euclidean semicircle horizontal chord span at fixed endpoint heights. The quotient shortest lift and independent area coordinates are proved; the change u=sqrt(H²-a²), v=sqrt(H²-b²) yields an exact simplex integral. Two Dirichlet simplex moments give both displayed coefficients; uniform Taylor bounds give O_w(\(H^{-10}\)). A uniform density ratio on a fixed compact marked domain gives O_w(\(H^{-2}\)) total-variation convergence. A portable checker independently tests 80,000 apex predicates and numeric integrals; those finite tests are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The canonical finite-geodesic event of entering a deep horocycle while both area-random endpoints remain below it has a non-obvious sixth-power tail from the double near-tangency layer. Its exact coefficient is a new inverse geometric fingerprint of cusp width; the second term and universal beta–Dirichlet marks resolve the rare excursion mechanism. The statistic is directly motivated by geodesic excursion geometry and not a routine parameter substitution into a distance distribution.
